summary: Cynthia Col is a sinology and religious studies scholar who studied Chinese religion at the Graduate Theological Union. She also studied under Steven D. Goodman and Mark C. Elliott in 1998.

Cynthia Talbot is a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology who studied at the University of Wisconsin–Madison from circa 1980 to 1988. Around 1993, she held an academic post at the University of Texas at Austin.

Cyril Henry Philips was an Indology and history scholar who studied at the University of Liverpool (circa 1930–1934) and SOAS (circa 1934–1936). He later served as Director of SOAS (circa 1956–1976) and held a post at the University of London (1972–1976).

Cyrus Stearns is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who earned his PhD at the University of Washington (circa 1985–1996) under Leonard van der Kuijp, among other teachers. Around 2004, he worked as a translator at the Tsadra Foundation.

Cécile Ducher is a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She completed her PhD under Matthew T. Kapstein at the École Pratique des Hautes Études (circa 2011–2017), where she later served as a research fellow around 2018.

D. C. Lau was a scholar of sinology and philosophy who studied at the University of Hong Kong from circa 1939 to 1946. He held posts at SOAS University of London (circa 1950–1978) and University College London (1970–1978).
D. C. Sarasvati is an Indology scholar who studied under V. Raghavan. From 1964 to 1965, Sarasvati held a position as Lecturer-cum-Research Assistant at the University of Madras.

D. Neil Schmid is a scholar of sinology and Buddhist studies who studied at Waseda University, the École Pratique des Hautes Études, and under Victor H. Mair at the University of Pennsylvania (circa 1995–2002).

Dagfinn Føllesdal was a philosopher who studied at the University of Oslo and at Harvard under Willard Van Orman Quine. He held posts at the University of Oslo (circa 1967–1999) and Stanford University (around 1968).

Dagmar Schwerk is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She studied at the University of Hamburg from circa 2008 to 2017, completing doctoral studies under Dorji Wangchuk between circa 2012 and 2017.
Daijo Tokiwa was a scholar of Buddhist studies and sinology who studied at the University of Tokyo from circa 1896 to 1899. He later held a post at Toyo University from circa 1904 to 1939.

Daiju Sasaki is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Taisho University from circa 1996 to 2007. Sasaki has held posts as an adjunct lecturer at Taisho University and as a full-time lecturer in sectarian studies at Chisan Denpoin.
Dainin Katagiri was a Buddhist studies figure who studied under Eko Hashimoto (circa 1946–1953) and at Komazawa University (circa 1948–1952). He founded the Minnesota Zen Meditation Center in 1972.

Daisetz Teitaro Suzuki was a Buddhist studies and philosophy scholar who studied at Waseda, the University of Tokyo, and under Paul Carus. He held posts at Otani University, Columbia University, Tokyo Imperial University, and Gakushuin, and founded Matsugaoka Bunko.
Daishun Ueyama was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology who studied under Akira Fujieda. He served as president during his academic career at Ryukoku University from circa 1968 to 2004.

Dale S. Wright is a scholar of Buddhist studies, philosophy, and religious studies who studied under Alan Anderson, Wang Pachow, and Robert Scharlemann. He served as Gamble Professor of Religious Studies and Asian Studies at Occidental College (circa 1980–2017).

Dalsukh D. Malvania was an Indology, philosophy, and Buddhist studies scholar. He held a post at Banaras Hindu University (circa 1949–1959), served as Director of the L.D. Institute of Indology (circa 1959–1977), and was a professor at Gujarat University (1979).
Damdin Badaraev is a scholar of Tibetology and linguistics who studied under George Roerich from circa 1957 to 1960 and under Bidya Dandaron from circa 1960 to 1972.

Damien Keown is a scholar of Buddhist studies, religious studies, and philosophy who studied at Lancaster University and the University of Oxford. He served as Emeritus Professor of Buddhist Ethics at Goldsmiths, University of London, and founded the Journal of Buddhist Ethics.

Damodar Dharmananda Kosambi was a history, archaeology, and Indology scholar who studied at Cambridge Rindge and Latin School, Harvard University, and Fergusson College. He held an academic post at Banaras Hindu University from circa 1930 to 1931.
